newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish erratic trade mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish erratic trade mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended a session of spotty trading mixed, with the long end recouping the bulk of morning losses and ending mainly on the plus side.
June Treasury bond futures hit day's highs late, with some traders saying the morning's breakdown below the seven-percent yield equivalent area near 108-05/32 may have drawn buyers.
"I saw some big buy orders down there," said one Treasury bond futures floor broker.
Other brokers mentioned market talk they said had circulated this week that fund managers and overseas investors were ready to scoop up U.S. Treasuries at seven percent.

But brokers said they thought Thursday's resilience in T-bonds emanated mainly from shortcovering and briefly drew power from buy stops, as that contract returned above the 108-00 area after probing lower.
Some said shorts were disappointed with the lack of downside extension after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan comments that many brokers viewed as hawkish.

Greenspan said the United States ideally must act pre- emptively to keep inflation low, if Fed acts next week the effect on inflation may not be felt for a while, and core CPI is likely to come under pressure from a tight labor market.
Brokers said they construed Greenspan's remarks as suggesting the Fed might tighten credit March 25.

"We have priced in a quarter point," said one Eurodollar broker. "We hit our low on stops and rallied back on short covering. I think a lot of what this (recovery) is, is the idea there will be a quarter point next week and no more."
Others said the curve flattened on technicals as well as ideas that a small Fed tightening might usher in a "relief" bounce up in price in the long end.
"I think you could at least see a point rally," said another T-bond futures floor broker.
Futures early showed muted initial response to U.S economic data. Weekly jobless claims rose 3,000 to 312,000 from a revised 309,000 and compared to forecasts for 316,000.

But January's U.S. trade deficit surged 21.1 percent to $12.71 billion, far above estimates for a $10.7 billion shortfall. It fostered talk of downward revisions in analysts' first-quarter gross domestic product estimates.
June T-bonds rose 6/32 to 108-21/32, T-notes lost 1/32 to 106-16/32, muni-bonds rose 9/32 to 113-09/32, Sept T-bills lost 0.045 bps to 94.385, and Eurodollars lost 0.045 to 93.825.
